subtitles.text:
Looking into the distance, humanity encountered something
that resembled what was most intimate within itself.

While analyzing minute refractions in light from distant galaxies,
researchers discovered a pattern that could not be explained
as a signal from any known celestial body or form of matter.

Similar structures were later detected by instruments on Earth
and showed a strong correlation with intense changes in human emotion.

This discovery led emotions to be understood not as
something confined to the individual, but as phenomena
that could leave traces in spaces beyond the body.

Researchers called the field formed as emotions
accumulated and overlapped in space a resonant field.

Yet it remained unclear whether resonant fields were formed solely
by human emotions, whether other beings also shaped them,
or how they were related to the patterns found in space.

Within resonant fields, different types of
unknown entities were repeatedly detected.

The entities could not be classified as any known species
and were thought to have existed long before their discovery.

What they were and why they were drawn
to resonant fields remained unknown.

The detector measured various changes occurring in space and
reconstructed the state of the entities from recurring patterns
within them, but their actual appearance remained unknown.

With repeated observation, the entities’
once-unstable patterns gradually became more consistent.

When observations decreased or the conditions of the resonant field changed,
the detected movements and patterns of repetition shifted,
while the signals sometimes weakened or dispersed again.

Before the nature of these entities was fully understood, personal
companion-entity detectors and service apps became widely available.
People began calling them companion entities.

The service apps translated the entities’
states into terms people could understand.

Signal strength, duration, distribution, and repetition were translated into
the language of personality, mood, intimacy, and attachment, transforming an
unknown phenomenon into a character that could be discovered and cared for on-screen.

People named their companion entities, recorded changes in their states,
and reached toward the points indicated by their detectors.
These gestures held both tenderness and interference.

As companion entities became widespread, the market
expanded into real estate and various services.

Companion entities were bound to the texture
of the resonant field accumulated in a particular place.

When registered users moved away, the same companion entity
could not be detected again in their new location.

Repeated detection records in a particular space became an indicator
of the likelihood that a companion entity would appear, and the real estate market
began promoting frequently detected spaces as premium properties.

Resonant fields were converted into spatial value, while
companion entities became objects for individuals to register and manage.

Companies sold subscription plans that stored observation records,
interaction data, and character models of companion entities.

The translations and records created to recognize unknown beings
became both a form of care and a means of ownership.

People realized that no space
was ever completely empty.

Humans were already entangled with the resonances of other beings,
and with or without a detector, no one could fully escape that entanglement.
The act of recognition changed the conditions of existence.
No one could place themselves outside the world.
People called this era the end of solitude.
